venue.name: Comox Valley Art Gallery
venue.description: The Comox Valley Art Gallery is an independent public gallery run by a non-profit society at 580 Duncan Avenue in downtown Courtenay. It shows contemporary art and runs all ages make art projects, youth training and mentorship programs, and a gift shop selling work by local artists. Admission is free and donations are appreciated. The gallery says it will book private or guided tours for small groups or classes.

facility_notes.washrooms: All facilities have gender-neutral signage, and one washroom is wheelchair accessible.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: CVAG spaces are accessible. The plaza has a ramp leading to the building entrance. Renovations in 2022 saw hallways widened and automatic push buttons installed on public doors.

restrictions: Children and those needing assistance must be accompanied by adult support persons.
We ask that visitors choose not to visit if they are experiencing symptoms of colds and flus.
venue.hours_notes: Wednesday to Saturday, 10:00am to 5:00pm. The gallery asks visitors to check its Facebook and Instagram for special hours and temporary closures.
venue.seasonal_notes: The exhibition spaces are temporarily closed for install until the next exhibition opens on Saturday, September 19, 2026, with doors from 10:00am. The gift shop stays open Wednesday to Saturday, 10:00am to 5:00pm.

programs.name: Guided tour for small groups and classes
programs.description: The gallery invites small groups and classes to contact it to book a private or guided tour of the exhibitions. Nothing is published about how long a tour runs, what ages it suits, how many children it takes, or how far ahead to ask, so all of that has to be settled by phone or email. Admission and programming at the gallery are free and donations are appreciated.
programs.what_children_do: Walk through the gallery spaces with a guide and look at the contemporary art in the current exhibition.
programs.our_note: Ring ahead rather than dropping in. The exhibition rooms close between shows, so the date matters more here than at most galleries. Nothing on their site says how long a tour takes or how many children they will take at once, so ask both.
programs.practical_summary: Toilets are on site and the building is step free, with a ramp up from the plaza and automatic door buttons. Somewhere to eat lunch and parking for a bus are not mentioned, so ask when you call.
programs.extra_fees_note: Admission is free and donations are appreciated. The site does not say separately whether a booked private or guided tour carries a fee.
programs.evidence: For general inquiries and to book private or guided tours for small groups or classes, contact us

programs.name: Make Art Projects
programs.description: Drop in art making sessions and workshops held at the gallery, tied to whatever exhibition is on at the time. Materials are provided and facilitators are on hand to give instruction. They are open to people of all ages and abilities and there is no charge, though children have to be accompanied by an adult. The gallery runs them on its own set dates rather than on request, so the events listings are the place to look for the next one. Recent sessions have been held in tents on the gallery plaza as well as indoors.
programs.what_children_do: Work at tables with materials the gallery supplies while a facilitator shows them how. Past sessions have included screen printing, painting a community mural, collage, making paper kites, lanterns and tie dye shirts.
programs.our_note: These run on the gallery's own dates, so it is not something you can book for a class on a morning of your choosing. If a date lines up with your week it is a genuinely good free outing. Ask whether the session is on the outdoor plaza or inside, because several of them are outside under tents.
programs.practical_summary: Materials, instruction, toilets and a step free building are all covered, and there is no cost. Lunch space, bus parking and how many children they can take at once are not stated.
programs.extra_fees_note: Participation is barrier-free (no cost); donations are appreciated. Materials are provided.
programs.evidence: Make Art Projects are open to people of all ages and abilities. Participation is barrier-free (no cost); donations are appreciated.

gaps: no ages or grades published for either offering; the gallery says only that Make Art Projects are open to all ages, so the app cannot show an age band
no duration for a guided tour or a Make Art session
no capacity for a booked group, and no minimum group size
no lead time or notice period for booking a group tour

no price is stated specifically for a booked private or guided tour; free was taken from the gallery's statement that admission and programming are barrier-free and no cost, which sits on the accessibility section rather than on a tours page
no lunch space, rain backup, stroller access or bus parking stated; the site mentions on-street parking and nearby parking lots but nothing about a bus
no chaperone ratio; the site says only that children must be accompanied by adult support persons
no days or times published for guided tours, so it is unknown whether they run outside the Wednesday to Saturday opening hours
the map embed on their location section carries only the map viewport centre and no place pin, so the point was derived from the published street address instead

alt text for both images was written by us after opening the image files in a browser and looking at them; both images have empty alt attributes on the site, and the captions beside them were used verbatim

the gallery also runs a STREAM Incubator for youth aged ten to fifteen and a Youth Media Project for ages sixteen to thirty, but both are registered programs for individuals rather than something a class or daycare can book, so neither is recorded as a program here
exhibition spaces were closed for install on the day this was checked and reopen on September 19, 2026, so a visit before that date would see the shop only
